text.p: The Canadian province of Quebec's budget deficit for the fiscal year 1995/96 was C$1.2 billion larger than it had reported, Quebec's auditor general said on Wednesday.
Guy Breton was quoted as saying Quebec used inappropriate accounting methods and left the cost of changes to the retirement plans for government employees out of its C$3.9 billion deficit.
"It represents 26 percent of the deficit. It's enormous," Breton told a legislative committee according to the Canadian Press.
Prior provincial governments used similar accounting methods but the 1995/96 fiscal shortfall was too large to overlook, Breton said according to the Canadian Press.
